{{verse|chapter=2|verse=1|align=float}}{{dropinitial|A}}{{sc|Nd}} I haue determined vvith my {{ls}}elf this {{ls}}ame thing, not to come to you againe in {{ls}}orovv. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2|align=float}}† For if I make you {{ls}}orie: and who is it that can make me glad, but he that is made {{ls}}orie by me? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3|align=float}}† And this {{ls}}ame I vvrote to you: that I may not, vvhen I come, haue {{ls}}orovv vpon {{ls}}orovv, of the vvhich I ought to reioyce: tru{{ls}}ting in you al, that my ioy is the ioy of you al. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4|align=float}}† For of much tribulation and angui{{ls}}h of hart I vvrote to you by many teares: not that you {{ls}}hould be made {{ls}}orie: but that you may knovv vvhat charitie I haue more aboundantly tovvard you. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=5|align=float}}† And if any man hath made {{ls}}orovvful, not me hath he made {{ls}}orovvful, but in part, that I burden not al you. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6|align=float}}† To him that is {{ls}}uch a one, {{sup|‖}} this rebuke {{ls}}ufficeth that is giuen of many: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7|align=float}}† {{ls}}o that cōtrariewi{{ls}}e you {{ls}}hould rather pardon and comfort him, le{{ls}}t perhaps {{ls}}uch an one be {{ls}}vvallovved vp vvith ouer great {{ls}}orow. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8|align=float}}† For the vvhich cau{{ls}}e {{sup|‖}} I be{{ls}}eeche you that you<noinclude>{{continues|confirme}}
